en.body: The fallback to one column below 52rem read @media (the window); a Questionnaire embedded in a narrow panel or Dialog on an otherwise wide page never fell back, even with no room for both. It is now @container, following decision 35, which the rest of the system already does; it still resolves correctly even inside a modal <dialog>.
en.title: The two columns fall back to one by the container, not the window

es.body: El retroceso a una columna bajo 52rem leía @media (la ventana); un Questionnaire embebido en un panel o un Dialog angosto sobre una página ancha nunca caía a una columna, aunque no tuviera lugar para las dos. Ahora es @container, siguiendo la decisión 35 que ya sigue el resto del sistema; sigue resolviendo bien incluso dentro de un <dialog> modal.
es.title: Las dos columnas caen a una por el contenedor, no por la ventana

en.body: Every QuestionnaireItem announces itself to Questionnaire no matter how many of your own components wrap it (a wizard step with its own chrome, say); before, the one-level walk of children could not see past the wrapper and the question was left out of the count, navigation and submit. shortcut: a wrapped item interleaved between two direct ones lands grouped after all the direct ones, not between them.
en.title: A QuestionnaireItem wrapped in your own component now counts

es.body: Cada QuestionnaireItem se anota a sí mismo ante Questionnaire sin importar cuántos componentes propios lo envuelvan (un paso de wizard con su propia cromática, por ejemplo); antes, el recorrido de un solo nivel de children no veía más allá del envoltorio y la pregunta quedaba fuera de la cuenta, la navegación y el envío. shortcut: un ítem envuelto intercalado entre dos directos queda agrupado después de todos los directos, no entre ellos.
es.title: Un QuestionnaireItem envuelto en un componente propio ya cuenta

en.body: Two new slots, shown inside the question as typography.css's own eyebrow role. Read fresh on every question in the group, never deduplicated against the one before: the questionnaire shows one question at a time, so there is no sibling beside it to repeat.
en.title: section / sectionDescription: a question group's own eyebrow

es.body: Dos slots nuevos, mostrados dentro de la pregunta como el rol eyebrow de typography.css. Se leen de nuevo en cada pregunta del grupo, nunca deduplicados contra la anterior: el cuestionario muestra una pregunta a la vez, así que no hay un hermano al lado para repetirse.
es.title: section / sectionDescription: el eyebrow de un grupo de preguntas

en.body: Before, only onValuesSubmit handed over answers, and only on a valid submit. A draft that saves itself listened to the <form>'s own change and re-read FormData by hand. onValuesChange reports the same value questionnaireValues already computes, on every change.
en.title: onValuesChange: every answer, valid or not, after every change

es.body: Antes solo onValuesSubmit entregaba respuestas, y solo al enviar con todo válido. Un borrador que se guarda solo escuchaba el change del <form> y releía FormData a mano. onValuesChange reporta el mismo valor que ya calcula questionnaireValues, en cada cambio.
es.title: onValuesChange: cada respuesta, válida o no, después de cada cambio

en.body: When free text is all a question asks for (no choices, no control and no textType), it is now a three-row textarea instead of one line: an open question needs room.
en.title: A question that only asks for free text is a textarea

es.body: Si el texto libre es lo único que pide una pregunta (sin choices, sin control y sin textType), ahora es un textarea de tres filas en vez de una línea: una pregunta abierta necesita espacio.
es.title: Una pregunta que solo pide texto libre es un textarea

es.title: Restaurado el scrollbar estándar del kit

en.body: The panel adds no scrollbar padding. A shared kit variant insets the thumb by 4 px at each end without shortening the track; unsupported browsers retain the standard scrollbar.
en.title: Full-height track with vertical inset on the thumb only

es.body: El panel no añade padding al scrollbar. La variante compartida del kit deja 4 px en los extremos del thumb sin acortar el track; sin soporte se conserva el scrollbar estándar.
es.title: Track completo con separación vertical solo en el thumb

en.body: Padding applies to items inside the list. The scrollbar reaches the panel's inner edge while its corners remain clipped.

en.body: selectedcontent truncates the value with an ellipsis while preserving the picker icon. React installs it after hydration; unsupported browsers keep the classic native control.

es.body: selectedcontent recorta el valor con puntos suspensivos y deja visible la flecha. React lo instala después de hidratar; sin soporte se conserva el control nativo clásico.
es.title: Valores largos en una sola línea, sin desbordar el campo

en.body: The outer panel owns padding and border. The list leaves the same gap before the scrollbar without overriding kit styling, including in RTL.

es.body: El panel exterior lleva el padding y el borde. La lista deja la misma separación antes del scrollbar, sin modificar los estilos del kit; también en RTL.
es.title: Espacio simétrico alrededor de la lista y el scrollbar

en.body: Native select uses sk-scrollbar, and the enhanced popup adds a rounded clipping panel without changing Zag's scrolling list. Select-specific scrollbar styling is removed.
en.title: Kit scrollbar in both selects

es.body: El select nativo usa sk-scrollbar y el desplegable mejorado añade un panel con recorte redondeado sin cambiar la lista que controla Zag. Se eliminan los estilos de scrollbar específicos del select.
es.title: Scrollbar del kit en ambos selects

en.body: Select now calls the same useFormFieldControl Input/NativeSelect already do. With no label of its own, the trigger takes the field's id (native association, no aria-labelledby) and no longer paints a second label. With its own label, Select's own pairing stays untouched.
en.title: Inside FormField, one label: Select now inherits id, required and describedBy

es.body: Select ahora llama al mismo useFormFieldControl que Input/NativeSelect. Sin label propio, el trigger toma el id del campo (asociación nativa, sin aria-labelledby) y ya no pinta una segunda etiqueta. Con label propio, el emparejamiento de Select con el suyo queda intacto.
es.title: Dentro de FormField, un solo label: Select ya hereda el id, required y describedBy

en.body: The contract already declared forward: ["id", "aria-*"], but the React binding silently dropped them. es.body: El contrato ya declaraba forward: ["id", "aria-*"], pero el binding de React los descartaba en silencio. Van al trigger real; si no se pasan, no tocan el aria-labelledby que Zag ya calcula. es.title: aria-label / aria-labelledby, un nombre accesible oculto

the content is compared across sections; folding forces remembering instead of looking

type=multiple: several can stay open at once, and they are still one accordion

useWhen: a section that expands and needs no JavaScript at all

avoidWhen: it is outside a Details; nothing opens it

avoidWhen: it is outside a Details; there is nothing for it to open
useWhen: it is what the closed state shows and what opens the section

avoidWhen: which one is open has to be controlled from outside, or its changes listened to: that needs Accordion
useWhen: several sections open and close, and letting the browser handle it is enough
only one should stay open: siblings sharing a name already do that on their own

a11y.because: un sujeto inerte sale del árbol de accesibilidad, así que sin `label` el grupo queda como una lista de nombres de partes sin decir de qué son las partes

avoidWhen: what is wanted is a numbered legend under a static image, with no leaders or rings: that is a List or a Table
the label has to appear on hover or focus: that is Tooltip, which is floating, ephemeral chrome; this is always drawn
a value next to a control inside a real form needs explaining: that is FormField's `hint`, which is also linked through aria-describedby
the subject has to stay usable: `inert` is all or nothing, so a diagram over a live UI is two things fighting over the same markup
the diagram is boxes and arrows between nodes, not the parts of one thing: this anchors each label to a selector inside the subject, it does not draw a graph
useWhen: the pieces of something already rendered have to be pointed at and named: a component's anatomy, the parts of a composition, an assembly diagram

the marks must not cover it: each part gets a number in one of the four margins of a grid and the subject takes the middle cell, so overlap is not avoided, it cannot be expressed; the names go in an ordered legend below
each number reaches its part by a leader line of one or two segments, straight or at 45 degrees only: the fewest that will do
the drawing recomputes itself when the container resizes, the subject reflows or a font arrives: where a part lands is not a value that can be written when composing
the diagram has to read on a phone: the drawing lives on a canvas, is designed at its own width and shown fitted, with zoom to get close to a part

some parts are areas that contain others (an accordion, one of its items, a panel): `mark: bracket` marks them with a bracket as long as the part, nested outward, instead of a leader that would land on some arbitrary child
the subject is a sample and not a control: `inert` is on, it takes no pointer, focus or keyboard, and leaves the accessibility tree

children.text: Use two fingers to move the view

it is a website's header with destinations; that is a Navbar
the menus sit among other controls on a page and should read as buttons; that is a Menubar
the actions are icons for the current selection; that is a Toolbar
there is a single menu of commands behind one button; that is a Menu
useWhen: the top edge of an application (an editor, a tool, a dashboard) needs its menus in one short line of text, the way a desktop OS draws its menu bar
the application also has a few words of state to keep in view (saved, a width, a zoom level, a clock) and some of them open a small menu

it is a short effect or a click on an interface action; a sound that answers a press needs no controls
there is a picture to watch; that is VideoPlayer, which has a stage, a poster and fullscreen
the app needs shuffle, repeat, a queue the reader reorders or lyrics; those are the app's policy, and this player moves along a list and nothing more
useWhen: a sound has to be played inside the page and its controls should look like the rest of the interface instead of the browser's own bar: a podcast episode, a song, a voice note, a recording
the reader should be able to run it from the keyboard alone: play, seek, volume, speed and the previous and next track all have a key, scoped to the player and never to the page
there is a list of tracks (an album, a set of episodes) and the player should load one, move on when it ends, and show which one is playing

the phone should offer to autofill the code received by SMS

avoidWhen: the list is short and fits whole; paging adds a step that buys nothing

the table already brings page size and row status; that is TablePager

the reader should be able to run it from the keyboard alone: play, seek, volume, speed, captions and fullscreen all have a key, scoped to the player and never to the page
the video is a file you host or link (an mp4 or webm with an optional poster and caption tracks); the player draws over a real video element and leaves the sources and tracks to you

a11y.because: An icon-only trigger shows no text, so the trigger button owns the accessible name; the glyph is decorative.

avoidWhen: something has to be decided before going on; that is a Dialog, which makes the page inert
the content hangs from a control and closes on an outside click; that is a Popover
the panel comes in from an edge and does not move; that is a Vaul
the content has to stay visible without JavaScript: a window does not open without its machine
useWhen: a panel has to live alongside the page: a tool palette, an inspector, a chat that stays open beside the work
whoever uses it has to be able to move it, resize it or minimize it to see what it covers

avoidWhen: the content should touch the edges (a full-bleed image or band); full still leaves gutters, so there is no wrapper there, or LayoutGrid with data-width="full-width" is used
some children should be narrower or wider than the rest; that is LayoutGrid, not nested Wrappers
it is already inside another Wrapper; nesting them adds both inline paddings and the outer ceiling wins anyway
the region needs a background, border or padding of its own; Wrapper only measures and centers, that is a Box (inside or outside the Wrapper)
useWhen: the page needs a centered measure so the text does not stretch edge to edge
a header, a body and a footer should share the same width ceiling: all three use the same wrapperSize
the content needs side gutters but no ceiling; that is wrapperSize full, which keeps the inline padding and only drops the maximum

vocabulary.a11y: When `when` holds, one of `requiresOneOf` must be given: an option, a raw attribute, a filled slot, or a child signature by name.
vocabulary.atLeastOneOf: At least one member of each group counts: a filled slot, a boolean option set to true, or an option other than its default.
vocabulary.authoredAttrs: Contract `authoredAttrs` publishes `data-sk-*` hooks an author writes on a host belonging to ANOTHER family (Vaul `data-sk-vaul-close` on a Button, Megamenu `data-sk-megamenu-preview` on a NavListLink). `data-*` outside `data-sk-*` is the author's namespace and needs no declaration; an undeclared `data-sk-*` is `unknown-attr`.
vocabulary.between: A number bounded by other options of the same node, inclusive; an omitted bound reads as its default.
vocabulary.childAttrs: Slot `childAttrs` names attributes a direct child may carry on its own host (LayoutGrid `data-width`). Authored on the child via UsageTree `attrs`; values are checked against each option.
vocabulary.compose: Signature `compose` lists families this signature borrows (`of` = contract id) via `also` / baked chrome / binding injection. Optional `sheets` must exist in the CSS corpus; `systemOwned: true` means the composed markup is not an authored UsageTree child.
vocabulary.contractSurface: Changelog `surface` hashes the public contract: css, parts, options (type/values/default/attr/prop/constraints/computedInput/…), events, eventDetails, a11y, hooks, hookSheets, outputHooks, authoredAttrs, systemOwned, and per signature host, option lists, requires/forbids/groups, parents, notInside, descendants, implies/excludes/pairs/slotImplies, slots, mount, portals, hitTesting, forward, compose, deprecated. Excludes template (also/attrs/attrsWhen/optionAttrs/…), wiring, because, intent, react, category, and option.machineInput.
vocabulary.descendants: Per group, at least `min` of the `of` signatures (counted together) sit anywhere below this node, through every slot and collection entry.
vocabulary.element: An enum whose value is the host element's tag instead of an attribute.

events.detail: `eventDetails[name].detail` is the fields of `event.detail` with TypeScript types.
events.direction: `direction: "in"` is a command the consumer dispatches; omit (or out) means the component fires it.
events.name: `events` maps the code name (`valueChange`) to the DOM name (`sk:accordionvaluechange`).
events.reactDetail: `reactDetail` is the React callback argument when it is not the `detail` object (bare value or `void`).
events.reactProp: `reactProp` is the React callback (`onValueChange`); `false` means no dedicated prop (DOM / handle / site-only).
events.source: `source` is the key of `parts` that dispatches (or listens for) the CustomEvent; usually `root`.
events.trigger: `trigger` is the key of `parts` the user activates to cause the event. Omit when several parts can fire it, for lifecycle/timeout, or for inbound commands.

vocabulary.exactlyOneOf: Exactly one option of each group is given.
vocabulary.excludes: When the key holds, no listed name may hold. Same key forms as `implies`.
vocabulary.forbids: No listed option may be given on this signature.
vocabulary.forward: Signature `forward` lists host attributes accepted via UsageTree `attrs`. When set, other attrs are `unknown-attr` (except `class`/`style`, any `data-*` outside `data-sk-*`, a contract's `authoredAttrs`, and a parent slot's `childAttrs`). A trailing `*` is a prefix (`aria-*`). Absent keeps attrs open.
vocabulary.given: An option is given when the tree sets it (a boolean only when true), a slot when it holds a composed child or non-blank text, a collection when it has an entry.
vocabulary.hitTesting: Signature `hitTesting` declares pointer hit-testing: `host: "none"` for the host itself, `childrenNone` for direct children of those signatures (BadgeHolder's Badge/BadgeDot) that receive `pointer-events: none`.
vocabulary.implies: When the key holds, every listed name must hold too. Keys and names are an option, a slot, or `option=value` (the omitted option reads as its default).
vocabulary.keyOf: A string naming entries of the signature's own keyed collection (`many`: space- or comma-separated); recursive collections are searched at every depth.
vocabulary.list: A string holding a list of positive numbers joined by `separator`; `countFrom` names the row whose children the length must match.
vocabulary.notInside: The signature may not sit inside any listed signature, at any depth.
vocabulary.optionAttrs: Template `optionAttrs` renames a host option's attribute on one node; an empty-string value omits that attribute on that node.
vocabulary.pairs: The option on the child composed into slot `a` equals the option on the child in slot `b`; a side with no value or default takes the other side's default.
vocabulary.pattern: A string matching the regular expression `source`.
vocabulary.portals: Signature `portals: true` means floating content leaves the subtree in React (Vanilla keeps it in place). `portals: { container: true }` also documents the React-only `container` ref that scopes the portal (default `document.body`).
vocabulary.refersTo: A string equal to the named option of some node of the named contract elsewhere in the same tree.
vocabulary.requires: Every listed option must be given (and a required string must not be blank).

severities.advisory: The rule cannot be settled from the tree alone, or the shape is legal but usually a mistake.

vocabulary.slotImplies: When the child in `when.slot` has `when.option` equal to `when.equals`, the child in `then.slot` must have `then.option` equal to `then.equals`. One-way, unlike `pairs`: the reverse need not hold. A side with no value takes its own default.

slotRules.cardinality: Per signature: `one` exactly one, `optional` at most one, `many` any number.
slotRules.countWhere: How many collection entries may have `option` equal to `equals`.
slotRules.flatHierarchy: Flat rows describe a tree through level, set size, position and expanded; the rows must agree.
slotRules.groupCardinality: The same counts over a group of signatures counted together.
slotRules.maxItems: Upper bound on composed children or collection entries.
slotRules.minItems: Lower bound on composed children or collection entries (checked once there is at least one).
slotRules.ordered: Children of the listed signatures appear in the order `of` lists them.
slotRules.positions: Positioned siblings share one set size and never repeat a position (set size -1 means unknown).
slotRules.restrictOptions: A child in this slot may only use the listed values for those options (booleans as "true"/"false").
slotRules.uniqueChildOption: Among composed signature children, the named option must be distinct (duplicate values are errors).

vocabulary.systemOwned: Contract `systemOwned` lists keys of `parts` that bindings/enhancers emit but authors never write in a UsageTree (Calendar grid, Carousel controls). Every name must be a key of `parts`.
vocabulary.valuesFrom: A string whose allowed values are another contract's option `values`.

when.present: `host.when` / `a11y.when`: the option is set to anything.
when.value: Any other value in `when`: the option equals it exactly.

vocabulary.whenGiven: Template node rendered only when the named option or slot is given; a list means any of them.
vocabulary.whenMissing: Template node rendered only when none of the named options or slots is given.
